subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs
messages:

Subject: Technical deep dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs

Alex / Priya — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + technical deep dive so we’re aligned on pain, goals, and next steps. I captured the key SLO requirements and a proposed deployment topology below. Please reply with any corrections.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Pain: inconsistent latency at peak (esp. Black Friday simulations). Current in-house inference has 300-800ms P95 for single-turn recommendation requests at 250 QPS.
- Business goal: sub-150ms P95 for user-visible recommendation generation at 200–300 sustained QPS during peak, predictable cost, and auditability for data access.
- Non-functional: strict data residency (US), SOC2 evidence required, and need for key rotation via customer KMS.

SLOs & targets discussed
- Latency target: 150ms P95 (single-turn generation, 2k token cap)
- Throughput target: 200–300 QPS sustained; 500 QPS burst for short periods (5–10 min)
- Availability target: 99.95% regional availability for production endpoints

Model & workload assumptions
- Model family: 13B encoder-decoder for recommendation reranking (open model candidate: LlamaX-13B or Mosaic-13B variant)
- Input sizes: median prompt ~200 tokens, 95th percentile ~1200 tokens for session histories
- Response sizes: median 40 tokens, occasionally up to 200 tokens for expanded explanations
- Quality constraints: beam-size 1 sampling with temperature 0.2 for ranking determinism; we discussed potential distillation/quantization if quality remains within acceptable thresholds.

Deployment topology options we discussed
1) Hosted Redwood (fastest to ship): multi-tenant with model variant pinned, prefix caching and workload-aware batching. Good for POC; predictable start-up but less isolation.
2) Dedicated (recommended for predictable peak throughput): reserved GPU pools with autoscaling policies, explicit capacity for sustained 250 QPS and burst handling. Allows KV cache warmers and pre-warmed workers.
3) Private (VPC) deployment: for strict compliance + KMS integration; same runtime but customer-managed networking.

Runtime optimizations we recommend
- Continuous batching tuned to 20–40ms aggregation window at 200 QPS to preserve latency SLOs
- KV cache for session histories (reduces redundant attention work for multi-turn)
- Quantization to int8/4 where acceptable; we’ll run evals to measure quality delta
- Tail-aware routing: route latency-sensitive traffic to lower-utilization pools; background batch jobs to cheaper capacity for lower-priority requests

Action items / next steps
- Redwood: deliver a short SLO matrix + proposed capacity profile and cost estimate (see attached redwood_slo_matrix.pdf). — Marissa (EOD Wednesday)
- Redwood: run model quantization quality evals on sample prompt set you shared. — Vivek (ETA 3 business days)
- Acme: confirm the sustained QPS target (200 vs 250) and provide sample 24-hour traffic trace (anonymized). — Alex / Priya
- Schedule a follow-up 45-min call to review cost and capacity profile.

Attachments: redwood_slo_matrix.pdf, mutual_action_plan.xlsx

Thanks — happy to sync quickly if anything above needs adjusting.

2) Traffic trace: I’ll extract an anonymized 24-hour trace from our infra and drop it into the shared folder by tomorrow EOD.
3) Model: we are open to trying Mosaic-13B but would like to compare latency/quality vs our internal distilled 8B model. Is it straightforward to host two variants (A/B) and route 10% traffic to the open model for evaluation?

Subject: Re: Technical deep dive recap: latency & throughput SLOs — technical notes

Alex / Priya — quick follow-up on the model A/B and HSM questions. Adding some concrete feasibility notes from the runtime side: 

A/B routing: yes — Redwood supports traffic-splitting by route. We can route a percentage of traffic to a secondary model variant for a fixed ramp (10% for N days) and capture per-route telemetry for quality and latency. We recommend doing the A/B as follows: 
- Warm KV cache for both variants with synthetic traffic before user traffic hits A/B
- Limit rollouts to consistent session buckets to avoid cache pollution

HSM / KMS: for Private (VPC) deployments we support customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations — we’ve done work with AWS CloudHSM and GCP HSM via customer key wrapping. We will need to validate network egress rules and key rotation policies during onboarding, but yes it’s supported.

Sizing and perf assumptions (back-of-envelope to validate Marissa’s matrix)
- Mosaic-13B (int8): single-GPU throughput ~120–150 tokens/s on A100-like instance with optimized kernels; with batching tuned to 20–30ms we estimate P95 generation in the 90–140ms band for 40–80 token responses at 200 QPS if KV cache hits are >= 60%
- Distilled 8B (float16): single-GPU throughput ~220–260 tokens/s; P95 could be lower (60–110ms) but quality must be validated on your ranking tasks
- For 250 sustained QPS with 200-token median context, recommended starting point: 4 workers (GPU instances) behind an autoscaler with buffer policies for burst to hit 500 QPS. We’ll refine this after we see the traffic trace.

Attachments: network_topology.png (sample dedicated capacity layout), quant_eval_template.csv

I’ll kick off the quantization eval on the sample prompts Marissa uploaded and share interim numbers in 48–72 hours.
